newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FIORENTINA AND BARCELONA EASE TOWARDS SEMIFINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIORENTINA AND BARCELONA EASE TOWARDS SEMIFINALS.

text.p: Fiorentina and Barcelona eased towards the semifinals of the Cup Winners' Cup with two-goal victories on Thursday but holders Paris St Germain and three-times European champions Liverpool had to settle for draws.
Fiorentina, winners of the inaugural Cup Winners' Cup in 1961, recorded the evening's most impressive result -- a 2-0 victory over Benfica in Portugal.

Argentine striker Gabriel Batistuta, who came into the game out of form in the Italian league, scored with a spectacular volley in the dying seconds to give the Italians a comfortable lead to take into the second leg in two weeks.
Batistuta had earlier laid on the first goal for fellow striker Francisco Baiano, slipping the ball to him on the edge of the box on the stroke of halftime.

Benfica, who won the European Cup in the year Fiorentina won their one and only Cup Winners' Cup title, are already out of the Portuguese title race and have a mountain to climb if they are to stay afloat in Europe.

Barcelona triumphed 3-1 at home to Sweden's AIK Stockholm after conceding a goal in the first minute thanks to a huge gaffe by reserve goalkeeper Carlos Busquets. He failed to control a backpass and gifted Pascal Simpson with the simplest of goals.
Gheorghe Popescu, Ronaldo and Juan Pizzi pulled the game round for the Catalans, bidding for their fourth Cup Winners' Cup title after their successes in 1979, 1982 and 1989.
Holders PSG failed to halt their alarming slump in form when they were held 0-0 at home by AEK Athens.
The Greek side's goalkeeper Ilias Atmatsidis made three crucial saves from Latin American pair Leonardo and Julio Cesar Dely Valdes to dash PSG's hopes of establishing a first leg lead.
Atmatsidis pushed out a point blank header by Panama striker Dely Valdes from a cross by Brazil's Leonardo only 50 seconds into the match, denying off-form PSG the early boost they dearly wanted.
PSG, in deep crisis since January, have not won a match at their Parc des Princes stadium since early November.
However, they are capable of recovering. In the last round they lost 4-2 to Galatasaray in the first leg before storming back to qualify 6-4 on aggregate.
Liverpool, in search of the only major trophy to have eluded them, took an early lead at Norwegian part-timers Brann Bergen but had to settle for a 1-1 draw to take back to Anfield.
Robbie Fowler scored a stylish opener after nine minutes but Brann, who knocked out Dutch league leaders PSV in the last round, equalised in the second half through Geir Hasund.
